brief: Raymond James' Monday morning note (Nov 16) ties three threads together. First, 3Q26 S&P 500 earnings are running +31% YoY, a third straight quarter of growth above 25%, but the beat margin has narrowed to 3.3%, the smallest since 4Q22; that tougher bar coincided with a 3% index pullback since earnings season began, even as 2027 consensus EPS growth was revised up to 16%. Second, October PPI came in cooler than expected month-over-month, but an upward revision to September, a 6.5% YoY producer-price pace (fastest since Nov 2022) and 4.9% core PPI (highest since 2022) reinforce the firm's call for a 25bp Fed hike on December 9; that, plus hawkish Fed commentary, drove the 2-year yield up 34bps and the 10-year up 28bps to 5.14% last week, repricing to more than three hikes by June 2027, though the firm still expects yields lower over the next year. Eleven Fed speakers, led by Chair Warsh, appear this week. Third, a data-center behind-the-meter power buildout (Aterio: 4GW to 188GW by 2031) supports the firm's constructive Industrials view, while retail sales and big-box earnings this week test consumer resilience.
